title: Page Number without Running Head

illustrates.quote: The alphabetic page number is placed on line 1 if there is no running head and on line 2 if there is a running head. The alphabetic page number is preceded by six cells of the page change indicator symbol (dots 36). Runovers are in cell 7.

page.features: Alphabetic page number scenario, no running head; numeric print page number 89 decoded from the braille numeral sign (a=1..i=9,j=0): #hi = h(8)i(9) = 89.

blocks.features: Schematic placeholder for generic body text ('text 444'); no real print excerpt is given -- illustrates alphabetic-page-number placement mechanics directly in braille.

braille.notes: Braille page lines 1-2, reconstructed to the stated 40-cell width (see example-1-7's identical extraction artefact: this line was 82 characters raw, right-tab-justified by the source .txt's own plain-text rendering rather than a literal one-space-per-cell count). No running head is used, so the alphabetic page number ('eighty-nine') is placed on line 1 by itself, preceded by six cells of the page-change-indicator symbol (dots 36, '------') and ending with the numeric page number '#hi' (89) at the right margin (6+9+22+3=40). Line 2 begins the body text placeholder.

resolution: Both runs agree on the braille content and on there being no real print excerpt to build from. Emboss has no spelled-out (alphabetic) page-number feature at all (standards-findings.md F-49) -- there is also no real print content behind the placeholder. status: not-representable (limitation: no print given, and F-49).
